<action type="say">
Yes, I can help you sort this out and decide how urgent it is.

First I need a clearer picture of what’s going on. Answer what you can; you don’t need to be technical:

1) Cooling performance
- Is your AC still blowing cool air, somewhat cool, or basically just room-temperature/warm air?
- Does it struggle more at the hottest part of the day, or all the time?

2) Airflow & noises
- Has the airflow from vents changed (weaker/stronger than usual)?
- Any new or unusual noises (grinding, squealing, banging, rattling, loud humming)?

3) Smells & leaks
- Any burning, chemical, moldy/musty, or “electrical” smells when it runs?
- Any water around the indoor unit, ceiling stains under it, or ice on any pipes/coils?
- Any visible oily spots near the outdoor unit lines (could suggest refrigerant leak)?

4) System behavior
- Does it short-cycle (turn on and off quickly) or run constantly without reaching the set temperature?
- Any recent error codes or blinking lights on a thermostat or unit?

5) Comfort & context
- Roughly how hot is it getting inside, and is anyone in the home elderly, very young, or with health issues?
- What city/region are you in (for climate), and is this central AC, a mini-split, or a window unit?

Once you share this, I’ll:
- tell you how urgent it likely is (safety, system damage risk, comfort), and
- translate your situation into the right kind of service request wording you can use when you call or book a tech.</action>

<action type="say">
From what you’ve described, this sounds like a non‑emergency performance/efficiency issue rather than something dangerous or urgent.

1) How urgent is it?
- Not an emergency: It still cools, no bad smells, no leaks/ice, no noises, no error codes, and indoor temps remain tolerable if you manage it.
- Worth addressing soon: The fact that it’s clearly weaker than last summer and struggles in late‑afternoon Phoenix heat suggests it likely needs maintenance or may be drifting out of spec (airflow, charge, or wear on components). If you wait, you’ll probably pay more in electricity and it could fail on a hotter day.

So this fits as a “routine HVAC service / diagnostic” you should book in the near future, not a same‑day emergency call.

2) Simple checks you can do yourself
Do these before or while you’re waiting for a visit:

- Filter:
  - If you haven’t changed the filter in the last 1–2 months, especially with Phoenix dust, replace it now.
  - A dirty filter alone can cause exactly what you’re describing (long run times, worse performance at peak heat).

- Thermostat:
  - Make sure it’s on “Cool” and fan is on “Auto” (not “On”).
  - If you have a cheap thermometer, hold it near a return vent and compare with thermostat reading; if it’s off by a couple degrees, that’s useful info for the tech.

- Outdoor unit:
  - Confirm there’s good clearance: about 2 feet around it, nothing blocking air.
  - Look at the coil through the side: if it looks matted with dust/yard debris, that can significantly hurt performance.

If after a clean filter and confirming clear airflow it’s still clearly weaker than last year (sounds like it is), booking service is reasonable.

3) What to ask a technician for (you can use this wording)
When you call or book online, you can say something like:

“I’m in Phoenix with a central AC in a single‑family home. The system is still cooling, but it doesn’t cool as fast or as cold as it did last summer. It runs a long time to drop just a couple of degrees and struggles more in the late afternoon when it’s hottest. Airflow seems normal. There are no odd noises, smells, leaks, or error codes. I’d like a diagnostic and maintenance check to see if there’s an issue with refrigerant charge, airflow, or any components, and to get it tuned up for the summer.”

If you’re choosing options in an online form:
- Service type: HVAC
- Visit type/reason: Routine maintenance / performance check (NOT “no cooling” or “emergency”)

4) If you’d like help scheduling
I can help you find and book someone. If you want that, tell me:
- Your ZIP code
- How soon you’d like service (e.g., “this week,” “next week,” or a specific date)
- Preferred time of day (morning / afternoon)
- Whether you prefer: best ratings, lower cost, or earliest availability

Then I’ll walk you through the next step and handle the details of what to request from the provider.</action>
